text:
Sam: quick heads-up — noticed a production tail-latency regression on the RAG chat workload after the latest runtime canary. p95 jumped ~2.4x for conversaion paths that use structured JSON output. Cache hit-rate for prefix cache dropped 87% -> 43% around 2026-03-15 02:10 UTC. attaching profiler snippet below.

Jia: 100% will be related to cache key entropy. can you paste how we're deriving the key?

Sam: sure, current key function is basically:
```
key = sha1(model + '::' + prefix_tokens_trunc16 + '::' + json.dumps(ctx_metadata))
```
ctx_metadata currently includes: conversation_id, turn_id, user_agent, client_ts, doc_ids (list), request_trace_id.

Jia: ok that explains it. `turn_id` and `request_trace_id` are per-request unique values -> exploding key cardinality. also doc_ids ordering varies across RAG callers. we should canonicalize doc_ids (sorted) and drop transient fields.

Ana: another wrinkle: structured outputs add inline provenance fields like {source: "doc-123", score: 0.87} baked into the prefix text, which changes tokenization and therefore the trimmed prefix_tokens_trunc16. even small metadata differences move token boundaries and cause misses.

Maria: from infra side: when hit-rate falls we see more long-context decoder runs (kernel path A) instead of the cached short-run (kernel path B). that triggers kernel swaps and a lot more GPU kernel launch overhead -> bulkier p95.

perf-bot: profile snapshot (canary-2026-03-15 02:11): p50=42ms p95=432ms p99=820ms | prefix_cache_hit=43% | prefix_cache_miss_tail=(>256ms) increased 3x. hot kernels: attention_forward_fp16, kv_load, matmul_large_seq.

Kyle: filing INF-2345 to track runtime + keying changes together. main thing: two-pronged approach IMO — (1) reduce key entropy (normalize/canonicalize), (2) warmup/prefetch for active convo sets so we avoid cold miss storm.

Jia: proposed canonical key rules:
- drop: request_trace_id, client_ts, turn_id
- normalize: sort doc_ids list, strip per-doc transient tokens (like version stamps)
- bucket: conversation_id -> conversation_bucket = sha1(conversation_id)[:8] to limit fanout for very chatty users
Final key example: `sha1(model + '::' + prefix_hash + '::' + sorted_docids_hash + '::' + conversation_bucket)`

Ana: warmup strategies to test:
- active-list prefetch: for each pod, background fetch top-N active conversation prefixes (LRU recency window), prioritize highest-QPS convos.
- pin-first-k: pin the first X tokens of a conversation prefix for 10 minutes after activity.
- staged prefetch: when user opens chat, async prefetch top-3 prefixes before first interactive call.

Maria: perf risk: prefetch increases memory pressure on the prefix cache and may cause thrashing if we over-prefetch. suggest a configurable budget per-pod and eviction grace for pinned entries. also add metrics: pinned_count, prefetch_evictions.

Kyle: can we make kernel selection less sensitive to cache miss bursts? i.e., if miss-rate > 30% use a fallback low-overhead kernel that favors latency over throughput until hit-rate recovers.

Sam: good idea. that would avoid the big kernel swap spikes. add to INF-2345 and assign to eng-runtime + eng-ml.

Jia: quick experiment plan:
1) rollout canonical key change in staging (A) and prod canary (B) on 10% traffic. measure prefix_cache_hit, p95 delta, unique-prefix-cardinality.
2) enable active-list prefetch on a separate canary group (C) with cache budget 200MB. watch eviction rate.
3) if (1) reduces card by >40% AND p95 improves -> roll. if (2) reduces p95 with eviction <5% -> consider production prefetch.

Maria: I'll add tracing spans to tag cache hits/misses with normalized_key vs legacy_key so we can A/B compare without losing historical lineage.

Ana: small code sample for doc_ids canonicalization:
```
doc_ids = meta.get('doc_ids', [])
clean_ids = [re.sub(r"^v\d+:", "", d) for d in doc_ids]
sorted_ids = sorted(set(clean_ids))
sorted_hash = sha1('\n'.join(sorted_ids))
```

Sam: cool. timeline? trying to get a quick mitigation before this week's peak.

Kyle: target: staging rollout of key normalization by EOD tomorrow, prefetch experiment mid-next-week. I'll sync with infra to reserve cache budget.

Jia: FYI, small edge-case: completions workload (non-chat) tends to have much lower key entropy because we only use a single prompt prefix per call. we shouldn't apply aggressive bucketing there. test matrix should include chat vs completion vs RAG.

Sam: noted. summary action items: INF-2345 created, PR draft for key canonicalization (WIP), prefetch experiment ticket, add cache metrics and kernel-fallback logic. thanks all. :thumbsup:

Maria: noted. tagging @oncall for visibility. :eyes:
